opening.argument: The call-center image identifies the scenario as “Apple Tech Support Phishing Scam,” framing the exchange as a phishing subject rather than a genuine support offer. In the depicted conversation, a speaker claims an iCloud breach and tells the recipient to press 1; another instruction directs the recipient toward a purported server and support website. Those instructions are presented as the speaker’s words, not attributed to the video’s creator. The abusive ending is consistent with an observed or documented interaction. The video therefore presents the support pitch as a subject of scrutiny, not as its own offer of help.
